title: One failure ladder for one-shot and warm turns; warm sessions degrade in place

body:
## Summary
The fleet's failure policy (what a rate limit, a bad login, an overload or a fatal error makes the engine do next) is written twice: once in `Fleet::complete` and again, differently, in `ClaudeWarmSession::send`. Extract it into one `ladder` module both paths consult, and let a warm session walk the same rungs: rotate accounts on rate-limit, auth and transient failures, then degrade in place to an API conversation that carries the session's own turns, reporting fleet mode on every served turn.

## Description
Today the warm path is a weaker copy of the one-shot ladder. A 529 overload or an auth failure on the warm account ends the turn with an error even when another account is healthy; when every account is cooling the warm session returns `RateLimited` instead of reaching the API rung that `open_session` itself would have used; and warm turns never call `set_mode`, so `FleetState` describes whichever one-shot ran last. The brain compensates at `crates/shadowrunr-brain/src/lib.rs:657-668` by catching every warm error and running a second, cold ladder, which doubles worst-case beat latency and throws the session away.

Techniques: agent-cli-transport / fallback-ladder (one labelled ladder, each rung tried only when the one above is honestly unavailable); multi-provider-gateway-plane / router-versus-candidate-failure (a candidate failure moves to the next candidate, a request failure stops the loop); agent-cli-transport / thread-custody-across-resume (the host keeps its own transcript mirror so a switch does not drop the thread).

The move:
- `ladder.rs`: `fn step(&Failure) -> Step { Rotate { cool: Option<Option<i64>> }, Stop(EngineError) }`, an `Attempts` value that collects elimination reasons, and `served(&FleetInner, EngineKind)` that sets the mode. `complete` and `open_session` use it.
- `ClaudeWarmSession` keeps a turn mirror (user prompt, assistant text) since open. `send` consults `step`; on rotation it moves account (as today, now also for Auth/Transient); when no account is left and the API is configured it switches its backend to an API conversation seeded from the mirror (the `ApiSession` body, reused), with `fallback_reason` set. A later `send` after the cooldown can return to a CLI account with a fresh process.
- Every successful warm turn calls `served`, so the mode is Primary/Degraded by what actually answered.
The brain's cold fallback stays (outside this context) but stops being the only route to the API.

## Flow
- send -> CLI turn on account a
- Failure -> ladder::step -> Rotate (cool a when told) -> next healthy account, same prompt
- no account left -> API backend seeded with the turn mirror -> reply, fallback_reason, mode Degraded
- Fatal -> Stop, returned unchanged
- success anywhere -> warm ledger row + served() sets mode

## Expected impact
One failure policy instead of two. A warm core thread survives an overload or a dead login on one seat without a dropped session and a second cold ladder. FleetState reflects warm turns, so the brain's sign-off clock reads what is actually answering. A new failure rule lands once.

## Evaluation
Claim: the warm path follows the same ladder as one-shot calls and reports fleet mode.
Before: 1 of 6 acceptance cases pass (only the Fatal regression guard)
After: 6 of 6
Method: gate - acceptance tests written first in tests/fake_cli.rs and ladder.rs
Result: better
Gate: architecture
evidence: fleet.rs:494-508 `match f { Failure::RateLimited {..} => { inner.cool(i, reset_at_ms); reasons.push(..) } Failure::Auth {..} => { inner.cool(i, None); reasons.push(..) } Failure::Transient {..} => reasons.push(..), Failure::Fatal(e) => return Err(e) }`; session.rs:367-371 `Failure::Auth { .. } => { self.inner.cool(self.account_idx, None); return Err(f.into_engine_error(self.account_label())); } other => return Err(other.into_engine_error(self.account_label()))`; session.rs:359-364 `_ => return Err(EngineError::RateLimited { account: from, reset_at_ms })`; `grep -n set_mode crates/shadowrunr-engine/src/*.rs` -> only fleet.rs:139,482,542,578,595,613,627,634; brain lib.rs:657-668 `Err(_) => { // The warm process died: fall back to a cold call, reopen next beat. self.session = None; ... } ... self.engine.complete(req).await`.

critic.reason: Real, verified duplication with a user-visible consequence (warm core dies on one bad seat); strong behavioural cases.

title: A live core turn queues behind a 15-minute judge: admit by lane, deadline at enqueue
acceptance: max_live_processes=2, live_reserved_processes=1, two Role::Judge one-shots on a fake account with delay_ms 1500 started first, then a Role::CoreThread complete -> the core reply returns in < 900 ms and the second judge is the one that waits (today: core waits >= 1500 ms)

rollback: admission.rs and the config key land first unused; then claude_cli/session/fleet switch to it; then the ledger field. Each is a clean git revert; the config key is optional and the ledger field is skip-if-zero, so old readers and configs are unaffected.

body:
## Summary
Every `claude`, codex and agy process the engine spawns waits on one global semaphore with no deadline, and the request's timeout starts only after the permit is granted. A 30 s core-thread turn can sit behind a 900 s judge, a 600 s reconciler or a 240 s research job, then still get its full 30 s. Split admission into a live lane (CoreThread, ChatPicker, Chatter) with reserved permits and a batch lane capped below the total, start the request's deadline at enqueue, and record queue time in the ledger.

## Description
This is the engine's process cap, not its model choice. The arrivals are not alike (a sub-second picker vs a quarter-hour judge), yet they share one line. Techniques: admission-queue / queue-cardinality (classes of work that need isolation get separate lines, not a priority knob on one); admission-queue / wait-telemetry (a fast executor reads as a slow one when the wait is not measured); model-call-outcome-integrity / one-deadline-across-attempts (one wall-clock budget computed when the call begins, every step spends from it).

The move:
- `admission.rs`: `Admission { shared: Arc<Semaphore>, reserve: Arc<Semaphore> }`, `fn lane(Role) -> Lane`, `async fn admit(&self, role, deadline: Instant) -> Result<(Permit, waited_ms), Expired>`. Live roles take the reserve or the shared lane, whichever frees first; batch roles take only the shared lane; the wait is bounded by the deadline.
- `ClaudeCli` holds `Admission` instead of `sem`; `run_once`, the warm `spawn` and `spawn_alt` admit with `Instant::now() + timeout_ms` and pass the remainder to their read timeout. A wait that exhausts the budget is `Failure::Fatal(EngineError::Timeout)`, ledgered like any timeout.
- `EngineConfig::live_reserved_processes` (default 2, clamped to max-1; with max 1 the single slot is shared, today's behaviour).
- `LedgerRow::queue_ms` (skipped when 0).

## Flow
- complete(req) -> deadline = now + timeout_ms
- admit(role, deadline): live -> reserve | shared; batch -> shared only
- waited past the deadline -> Timeout row with queue_ms
- permit -> spawn, read with the remaining budget -> reply row with queue_ms

## Expected impact
The live voice can no longer be starved by the show's own background work (research jobs, sleep-cycle consolidation, a sim's judge and chatters on the same fleet). A core turn's 30 s means 30 s from when it was asked, so the brain's stall cover and fleet-loss policy see a bounded call. Queue time becomes visible in the ledger rows the console pages.

## Evaluation
Claim: live roles are admitted ahead of batch work and the timeout covers the wait.
Before: 0 of 6 acceptance cases pass (no lanes, no queue deadline, no queue_ms field)
After: 6 of 6
Method: gate - acceptance tests written first in tests/fake_cli.rs (fake CLI delay_ms) and admission.rs unit tests
Result: better
Gate: architecture
evidence: claude_cli.rs:238-245 `let _permit = self.sem.clone().acquire_owned().await.map_err(..)?;` then claude_cli.rs:287 `match tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_millis(req.timeout_ms), read).await` (the timeout wraps only the read); session.rs:162-169 same acquire, permit kept in LiveProc._permit (session.rs:47); fleet.rs:297-304 same acquire for alt CLIs; `grep -n acquire_owned crates/shadowrunr-engine/src/*.rs` -> claude_cli.rs:241, fleet.rs:300, session.rs:165 (all on ClaudeCli.sem); config.rs:85 `DEFAULT_MAX_LIVE_PROCESSES: usize = 6`; config.rs:16 CoreThread 30_000, :22 Judge 900_000, :23 Reconciler 600_000.

critic.reason: Verified head-of-line blocking of the live voice behind batch roles; concrete, testable fix.
